stimulus.source_note: Original summary; Fort Caroline built 1564 by French Huguenots under Laudonniere, destroyed by Menendez 1565; St. Augustine founded 1565.
stimulus.text: Spanish forces destroyed the French Fort Caroline in 1565 and immediately established the fortified town of St. Augustine on the Florida coast.

stem: Spain founded St. Augustine, Florida, in 1565 — the oldest continuously inhabited European-founded city in the continental United States. Which broader development best explains why Spain established a fortified settlement there at that time?

options.text: The need for a port to ship Potosi silver directly to Spain
Competition with France, whose Protestant colonists had built Fort Caroline nearby
The discovery of gold deposits in Florida
Spain's desire to establish a fur-trading partnership with Florida's Native peoples

instruction: Pick one option from the stimulus and stem only. Do not open the question file.
